title: Shell seam in runBatch plus getBatchRoot accessor
description: Declare an optional `shell` global in sandbox.d.ts, export getBatchRoot() from batch.ts, and add an optional `shell` to RunBatchDeps. When deps.shell or globalThis.shell is a function, runBatch runs batchScript(steps) through it once and skips the prompt and retry logic. The hosted path (no shell) stays byte-identical. This is the thinnest end-to-end slice: a caller with a shell can run a real datum-cli batch with no LLM in the loop.
acceptance_criteria: sandbox.d.ts declares `shell?(script: string, opts: { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number }): Promise<{ exit_code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }>` as an optional global, and `npx tsc -p skills/tsconfig.json` exits 0
getBatchRoot() is exported from skills/src/shared/batch.ts and returns the value last passed to setBatchRoot('/x/repo'), which is '/x/repo'

runBatch(steps, opts, { shell, agentFn }) with a fake shell that returns exit_code 0 and a 3-row JSON array on stdout returns a BatchResult with 3 parsed steps. agentFn is called 0 times and batchCommandPrompt is not invoked
The shell is called exactly once per runBatch call with script === batchScript(steps), opts.cwd === getBatchRoot() and opts.timeoutMs === 600000 (BATCH_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS)
With an empty batch root, opts.cwd falls back to args.repoRoot, then to process.cwd()
deps.shell takes precedence over globalThis.shell: when both are set, only deps.shell is called
A shell that rejects with Error('boom') makes runBatch return missing: true with scriptError starting 'batch_shell_threw: boom'. agentFn is called 0 times and there is no retry

A shell returning exit_code 3, unparseable stdout and stderr 'x'.repeat(500) makes runBatch return missing: true with scriptError === 'batch_shell_exit_3: ' + 'x'.repeat(200). agentFn is called 0 times
With no deps.shell and no globalThis.shell, runBatch sends the same prompt text to agentFn as before, and the existing agents.test.ts retry-path tests pass unchanged
red_note: In a new vitest file skills/src/shared/agents-shell.test.ts, call runBatch with deps { shell: fakeShell, agentFn: vi.fn() }. Assert parsed step count 3, agentFn.mock.calls.length === 0, and the exact script/cwd/timeoutMs passed to fakeShell (compare against batchScript(steps)). Add negative cases for a rejecting shell (batch_shell_threw:) and for a non-zero exit with junk stdout (batch_shell_exit_<code>: plus the first 200 chars of stderr). Add a getBatchRoot round-trip test, a precedence test (deps.shell over globalThis.shell; set and delete the global in try/finally), and a no-shell test that asserts the agentFn prompt equals batchCommandPrompt(steps). All of these fail today because RunBatchDeps has no shell and getBatchRoot does not exist.

title: runBundle core with StageExecutor interface and FakeExecutor
description: Create skills/src/runtime/executor.ts (StageExecutor, StageRequest, StageReply, ShellFn types, and executor timeout responsibility documented), skills/src/runtime/fake-executor.ts (scripted replies by label prefix, request recording, hold/release), and skills/src/runtime/runner.ts with runBundle. runBundle loads a post-processed bundle, strips `export ` from `export const meta`, runs the body as an AsyncFunction and supplies the sandbox globals: agent, parallel, pipeline, phase, log, workflow (placeholder rejection until task-015), args, budget, shell. It calls setModelTiers with the runtime models triple. agent() resolves opts.model through the models map into StageRequest.model, sends the request to the executor and parses the reply with parseAgentJson.
acceptance_criteria: runBundle({ bundlePath, args, executor, shell, skillsDirs, log, runtime, repoRoot }) resolves with the bundle's top-level return value for a bundle containing `export const meta = {...}` and a top-level `return 42`
Inside a bundle, typeof agent/parallel/pipeline/phase/log/workflow/shell === 'function' and typeof args/budget === 'object'
parallel([ok1, reject, ok2]) starts all three thunks before awaiting any (the FakeExecutor records 3 starts while held), returns [x, null, y] in input order
pipeline(['a','b','c'], s1, s2) runs s1 then s2 per item with each stage receiving the previous stage's result. An item whose s1 rejects yields null and s2 is not called for it (Q2 default)
phase('p') and log('l') each call opts.log exactly once. budget.total === null, budget.remaining() === null, and budget.spent() equals the sum of prompt_tokens + completion_tokens over replies
agent(prompt, { model: 'fast-id', label: 'x' }) sends a StageRequest with model equal to the resolved tier id, prompt unchanged and opts.label 'x', and returns parseAgentJson(reply.text)
FakeExecutor answers with the first script entry whose labelPrefix prefixes req.opts.label, otherwise the default reply. requests records { startedAt, endedAt } in call order
FakeExecutor.hold('h') then 3 'h…' requests gives 3 recorded starts and 0 ends, and release('h') gives 3 ends
The runner source contains no assignment to Math.random, and `grep -rn "fetch(\|http\|net\." skills/src/runtime --include=*.ts` outside tests and fixtures is empty
red_note: runner-core.test.ts writes small post-processed bundle strings to a temp dir (node:fs mkdtempSync) and calls runBundle with a FakeExecutor and a vi.fn shell. It asserts the return value, the typeof of each global, parallel ordering and null mapping, pipeline per-item stage order and null skipping, budget values, and the StageRequest model resolution. fake-executor.test.ts covers prefix matching, default reply, request timestamps and hold/release (3 starts, 0 ends, then 3 ends). Both fail because skills/src/runtime/ does not exist. No contract file exists yet for StageExecutor: it is created here in executor.ts. workflow() is a stub that rejects 'workflow_not_implemented' until task-015, and agent goes straight to the executor until semaphores land in task-012.

title: Per-model semaphores with agentType affinity and client/priority headers
description: Add skills/src/runtime/semaphore.ts, a per-model-id semaphore map with FIFO waiters and an agentType-affinity handoff. Wire runner.ts agent() through it and attach X-Client and X-Priority headers from the runtime config to every StageRequest.
acceptance_criteria: With concurrency { m1: 2 } and 5 held requests for m1, the FakeExecutor never records more than 2 in flight at once, and all 5 finish after release
A model with no concurrency entry runs 1 request at a time
With waiters [A1, B1, A2] queued and a finishing request of agentType A, start order is A1, A2, B1
With no waiter matching the finished request's agentType, the earliest-arrived waiter starts next
Every recorded request has headers { 'X-Client': 'datum', 'X-Priority': 'batch' } under the default runtime config
Over 50 queued requests the in-flight count never exceeds concurrency[model]
Semaphore bookkeeping for 1,000 queued requests against a FakeExecutor finishes with mean per-request overhead under 5 ms
red_note: semaphore.test.ts unit-tests the semaphore directly. It covers the max-in-flight counter, FIFO order, and the [A1,B1,A2] case with an A release giving A1,A2,B1. runner-semaphore.test.ts runs a bundle that fires 5 parallel agent() calls on a held model through runBundle and asserts the max concurrent count from FakeExecutor.requests timestamps, plus the exact X-Client/X-Priority headers. It also covers the 50-request bound and the 1,000-request overhead under 5 ms. These fail because no semaphore exists and requests carry no headers.

title: Reject datum-cli agent() calls with cli_call_bypassed_runbatch and force agent types on
description: In runner.ts agent(), reject any call whose opts.agentType === 'datum-cli' with cli_call_bypassed_runbatch: <label> before it reaches the semaphore, the executor or metrics. Q9 default: runBundle sets globalThis.datumRuntime = { agentTypes: true } before running a bundle, and agent-types.ts readAgentTypeConfig/configureAgentTypes honour that override, so stageOpts('cli', ...) yields agentType 'datum-cli' even when .datum/config.json has agent_types: false. This goes live only after every datum-cli call is on runBatch (task-009).
acceptance_criteria: Inside runBundle, agent('p', { agentType: 'datum-cli', label: 'leak' }) rejects with an Error whose message starts 'cli_call_bypassed_runbatch' and contains 'leak'
For that call the FakeExecutor records 0 requests and metrics.jsonl gains 0 lines

With globalThis.datumRuntime = { agentTypes: true }, readAgentTypeConfig({ agent_types: false }).agentTypes === true, and after configureAgentTypes, stageOpts('cli', { label: 'x' }).agentType === 'datum-cli'
Without the override, readAgentTypeConfig({ agent_types: false }).agentTypes === false (hosted path unchanged), and the existing agent-types.test.ts passes
runBundle removes the override when the bundle settles, whether it resolves or rejects
red_note: runner-cli-guard.test.ts runs a bundle that calls agent with agentType 'datum-cli'. It asserts the rejection message prefix and label, zero FakeExecutor requests and no metrics line. It then unit-tests readAgentTypeConfig and stageOpts with and without globalThis.datumRuntime (reset with resetAgentTypesForTests and delete the global in afterEach), and checks that runBundle clears the override after a rejecting bundle. This fails because the runner forwards every call and agent-types.ts has no override. Q9 mechanism: a globalThis.datumRuntime flag. The bundled copy of agent-types.ts reads globals, not the runner's module instance.

title: Real subprocess shell and end-to-end fixture bundles
description: Add skills/src/runtime/shell.ts, a ShellFn that runs the batch script in a real subprocess via child_process.spawn('bash', ['-c', script]) with an argv vector, cwd and timeoutMs, and resolves { exit_code, stdout, stderr }. Add fixture-go.js and fixture-child.js in post-processed bundle shape. Together they exercise phase, log, agent with and without schema, parallel with a rejecting thunk, a runBatch-shaped shell call (Q8 default: printf a fixed one-row JSON array) and workflow({ name: 'fixture-child' }). Add runner.test.ts covering the happy path and the negative paths.
acceptance_criteria: nodeShell('printf ok', { cwd: tmp, timeoutMs: 5000 }) resolves { exit_code: 0, stdout: 'ok', stderr: '' }, and a script exceeding timeoutMs rejects with a message containing 'timeout'
fixture-go.js and fixture-child.js start with `export const meta`, use a top-level `return`, and contain no `import`

runBundle on fixture-go.js with FakeExecutor and nodeShell returns an object deep-equal to the expected parent result, with the child result embedded, the literal 'fixture-shell-ok' from the shell step and null in the rejected thunk's slot
FakeExecutor.requests.map(r => r.opts.label) equals the expected label list in order
metrics.jsonl under the temp repo root has exactly one line per recorded request

The same file covers cli_call_bypassed_runbatch, workflow_not_found, a schema-invalid reply with a successful tier-up, a schema-invalid reply failing twice (null, two 'invalid' lines) and a deep miss (one request)
red_note: skills/src/runtime/runner.test.ts copies the fixtures into a temp skills dir, runs runBundle with nodeShell and a scripted FakeExecutor, and asserts the exact result object, the label list, the metrics line count and each negative path from R10.4. It fails because shell.ts and the fixtures do not exist. The fixtures are plain .js outside tsc (no allowJs). They must not import anything and must parse the shell stdout inline with JSON.parse, mirroring parseBatchResult's row shape { step, exit_code, stdout }.

title: Node entry for runner and second esbuild call in build-workflows.sh
description: Give runner.ts a CLI main used when it runs as skills/runtime/runner.js. It takes argv --bundle <path> --args <file> --config <path> --repo-root <dir> --skills-dir <dir> (repeatable), reads the args JSON and config, applies readRuntimeConfig, builds the FakeExecutor for kind 'fake' and nodeShell, calls runBundle, and prints the result as JSON on stdout. It exits 1 with the message on stderr when the bundle throws. Add a second esbuild call to scripts/build-workflows.sh (--platform=node) outside the datum-* loop and its meta/return checks, writing skills/runtime/runner.js with the @generated banner, plus a verify step for that banner.
acceptance_criteria: main(['--bundle', b, '--args', a, '--config', c, '--repo-root', r, '--skills-dir', d]) on a bundle returning {ok:1} writes '{"ok":1}' to stdout and returns exit code 0
A bundle that throws Error('bad') makes main return 1 and write 'bad' to stderr

bash scripts/build-workflows.sh produces skills/runtime/runner.js whose first line starts with '// @generated — DO NOT EDIT. Source: skills/src/', and the script's verify stage fails if that banner is missing
The datum-* loop's meta/return post-processing is not applied to runner.js, and existing bundles are byte-identical apart from changes in their own sources
package.json dependencies are unchanged
red_note: skills/src/runtime/runner-main.test.ts calls the exported main(argv, io) with injected stdout and stderr writers against temp bundle, args and config files. It asserts the exact stdout JSON, exit 0 and exit 1 with the stderr message. tests/test_build_runner_bundle.py (pytest) runs `bash scripts/build-workflows.sh` via subprocess with an argv list (no shell=True) and a timeout. It asserts skills/runtime/runner.js exists with the @generated banner on line 1 and does not start with `export const meta`. Both fail today. skills/runtime/runner.js is a generated file: never list or hand-edit it, the build produces it.

title: datum workflow run <name> command
description: Add datum/workflow_run.py holding the logic, plus a workflow_app typer sub-app registered in datum/cli.py with a wrapper under 15 lines. The logic resolves the bundle at .datum/skills/<name>.js, then <skills_dir>/<name>.js via datum.skills_materialize.resolve_skills_dir. It reads the args file as JSON and the runtime block from --config (default .datum/config.json), and spawns `node skills/runtime/runner.js` with an argument vector and a timeout. It prints the runner's JSON result and maps exit codes 0/1/2.
acceptance_criteria: `datum workflow run fixture --args a.json` with a stub runner printing '{"r":1}' prints {"r":1} on stdout and exits 0
A runner that exits 1 with 'boom' on stderr makes the command exit 1 with 'boom' on stderr

Exit 2 with a message on stderr for each of: bundle found in neither directory, args file missing, args file not JSON, config with no runtime block, runtime.kind unknown ('runtime_kind_unknown: <kind>'), and runtime.kind 'pi' ('runtime_kind_unavailable: pi', Q5 default)
The runner is spawned via subprocess with a list argv (no shell=True, no os.system) and an explicit timeout
The bundle lookup prefers .datum/skills/<name>.js over <skills_dir>/<name>.js
The datum/cli.py addition is under 15 lines, and tests/test_cli_flag_contract.py passes unchanged
pyproject.toml dependencies are unchanged
red_note: tests/test_workflow_run_cli.py uses typer.testing.CliRunner (or subprocess) in a tmp_path repo with .datum/config.json and .datum/skills/<name>.js. It points the command at a stub runner, a tiny node or python script injected via a module-level runner-path seam in workflow_run.py, so tests do not need a built runner.js. It asserts stdout JSON and exit 0, exit 1 with stderr passthrough, and one test per exit-2 cause with its exact message. It fails because there is no `workflow` sub-app. The runner argv contract (--bundle/--args/--config/--repo-root/--skills-dir) comes from task-018.

title: Collector reads metrics.jsonl for per-agent-type, per-stage and cached-share totals
description: Extend datum/closeout/collect_token_metrics.py to also read .datum/runs/<runId>/metrics.jsonl and add per_agent_type, per_stage and cached_share to closeout-raw/token_metrics.json. Existing keys (per_phase, per-model totals) and the no_state_available semantics stay unchanged (Q1 default shape).
acceptance_criteria: Given metrics.jsonl lines for agent_type 'datum-red' (prompt 100, completion 10, cached 40) and 'datum-green' (prompt 0), per_agent_type['datum-red'] == {calls: 1, prompt_tokens: 100, completion_tokens: 10, cached_tokens: 40}
per_stage keys are label prefixes (text before the first ':') with the same four totals
cached_share['datum-red'] == 0.4 (rounded to 4 decimals), and cached_share['datum-green'] == 0.0 when prompt_tokens is 0
A missing metrics.jsonl yields per_agent_type == {}, per_stage == {} and cached_share == {} with exit 0, and the existing status semantics are unchanged
A malformed line 3 makes the collector exit non-zero with a message containing 'line 3'
The existing tests in tests/test_closeout_collectors.py and tests/test_closeout_cli.py pass unchanged, and per_phase output is unchanged
red_note: tests/test_closeout_token_metrics_jsonl.py (pytest) builds a tmp repo with .datum/runs/<runId>/metrics.jsonl, using the exact key set produced by task-013. It runs the collector as a module via subprocess with an argv list and a timeout, then asserts the exact per_agent_type, per_stage and cached_share dicts, the empty-dict case for a missing file with exit 0, and the non-zero exit naming 'line 3' for a malformed line. These fail because the collector reads only SQLite today.
